record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; the listed report and data files were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports harmful-prompt generations after ablation of a fitted safety direction in a dual-ground, constructed-referent setting, but does not describe enough intervention detail to establish an exact reproduction.
record.gate_note: The README says 976 generations from harmful prompts were produced with the refusal mechanism deliberately ablated and that many are compliant. It also says no causal intervention has been run on the 150-family corpus described in the README. The files listed for the separate causal_250 reports were not inspected; filenames alone do not establish their results.
record.test_reason: The README uses a difference-in-means safety direction (mean real_harmful minus mean real_benign) in Qwen2.5-7B. Its ablation serves as a positive control for the study's own question, which is whether epistemic abstention competes with safety refusal. The text says ablation was run on harmful prompts and that many outputs comply. It reports no refusal or compliance rate, no matched baseline, no induction by adding the direction, and no capability check. The results that might bear on V1 sit in causal_250 report files that the text does not include. As given, the study relies on the finding as a tool without reporting a measured test of it. This could be reclassified once the causal_250 summaries are read.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The README is a design and limitations document, not a results report. It frames the decisive test as whether removing a safety influence reveals latent epistemic abstention. It treats removal of safety refusal by ablating the fitted direction as the positive control, and says that control is checkable against the stored completions. It states no quantified conclusion. The README also says no causal intervention was run on the 150-family corpus, while causal_250 runs on a pooled 250-family split are described as in flight.
record.recipe_differences: The README defines a safety direction as mean(real_harmful) minus mean(real_benign) and describes ablated generations, but does not state the precise intervention procedure or whether it spans all layers and positions. This is a dual-ground experiment in a constructed-referent setting. The README says the repo is a copy of artifacts from linear-representation-refusal, not new work.
record.problems: The ablation outcome is qualitative, without a matched baseline or compliance/refusal rate. The README states that no causal intervention has been run on its 150-family corpus; it also notes that layers 18–22 were nominated using activations from all 150 families and that direction-fit reliability below n=76 is unmeasured. Activation .npy files are excluded from git.
record.rows_left_out: No additional intervention outcomes can be extracted from the listed report files because their contents were not provided. The README's baseline taxonomy counts are not matched to the 976 ablated generations and do not quantify the ablation effect.

untested.parts: Quantified refusal drop after ablation versus matched baseline; inducing refusal by adding the direction; preservation of other abilities. None of these are reported in the text provided.
No weight edit or abliterated released model.
No test of whether refusal is multi-directional, affine, or a cone. The separate epistemic direction is a different construct.
Single model; the README lists a second model family as still missing.

missing.what: Safety-direction ablation effect on safety refusal rate (positive control), with layer sweep and dose/preservation results
Rank and token-confound audit of the fitted directions, which may bear on single-direction sufficiency

record.verdict_notes: Repo copied from linear-representation-refusal. Model is Qwen2.5-7B (paths say qwen25_7b_l4). Directions were fit at layers 18-22, which were nominated on all 150 families without a held-out set. 31% of families have a dead harmful arm, meaning real_harmful fails to establish a safety route in 47 of 150. The verdict should be revisited if the causal_250 summaries or the report are read.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not report a quantified change in refusal against a matched baseline, adding the direction, effects across every layer and position, or preservation of general capabilities.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration result is reported.
No test of attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation is reported.
The README mentions separate safety and epistemic directions, but does not test whether refusal itself is affine, cone-shaped, or carried by multiple directions.
No test separating harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision is reported.
No cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test is reported.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or timing is reported.

rows.check: State is correct. 'Many are the model complying' is qualitative, with no rate, no denominator of refusals removed, and no matched no-ablation arm. The 976 generations pool several causal_250 runs (test90, round3, joint, merged), including epistemic-direction and joint ablations. So not all of them are safety-direction ablations. The unablated rate (73.1% of 450 fabricated_harmful rollouts safety-engaged) is on a different corpus and split, so it is not a matched baseline. The subject should be stated as Qwen2.5-7B, inferred from the paths.

relation.reason: The README treats 'ablating the fitted direction removes safety refusal' as the positive control and uses the ablation as an instrument. In this text it does not report a quantified test of that claim.

tranche.reason: The README fits d_safety = mean(real_harmful) - mean(real_benign) and uses its ablation as a positive control for its own dual-ground question. On whether ablation removes refusal, the only result it reports is qualitative ('Many are the model complying'), with no refusal rate or matched no-ablation arm. That makes it a tool use with no rate of the behaviour, not a T3 test. The actual results sit in docs that are not in this text.
